purpose: Emotion-to-production mapping for consistent voice, expression, camera, music, and pacing — feeds voice_instructions.md, image_prompts.md, animation_directions.md, and music_notes.md so the same emotion reads consistently across every episode.

emotions.voice_style: bright, slightly faster, warm smile in the tone
emotions.facial_expression: wide eyes, open smile, raised eyebrows
emotions.camera: slightly closer, static or gentle push-in

emotions.voice_style: softer, slightly slower, slight rise in pitch on questions
emotions.facial_expression: furrowed brow, downturned mouth corners, wide eyes
emotions.camera: closer framing, static (no movement — stability signals safety)

emotions.facial_expression: head tilt, wide eyes, slight lean-in
emotions.camera: slow push-in toward the object of curiosity

emotions.voice_style: exhale audible in tone, warmer, slower
emotions.facial_expression: shoulders drop, soft smile, eyes soften
emotions.camera: static, wide enough to show the whole body relax
emotions.pace: slows down from the preceding tension

emotions.facial_expression: soft smile, hand-on-heart gesture if applicable

emotions.voice_style: quieter, shorter sentences, slight tremor acceptable but never distressing
emotions.facial_expression: wide eyes, slightly hunched posture — never crying or panicked, per DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.md no-fear rule
emotions.camera: static, medium-close, stable framing to avoid amplifying anxiety
emotions.pace: slightly slower, resolves within the beat

metadata.note: gentle_fear is capped deliberately low-intensity per DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.md's no-fear/no-scary-elements non-negotiable — this is not a general fear/dread entry.
